gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-old-tur: Refined and spread out, Stentiga lets its widely tracked capitals drift across the line, while Noto Sans Old Turkic sits below with chunky, tall lowercase. Try it big.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Every stroke in Stentiga is drawn with the same unmodulated line, like wire bent into letters. And Noto Sans Oriya answers with generous curves and small letters nearly as tall as its capitals.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Noto Sans Osmanya reads wide and easy, its lowercase oddly large beside the capitals. Over a full page that oversized body keeps the eye moving smoothly, while Stentiga's blunt marker-tip heading stays out of its way.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-: Stentiga cuts every letter at a single depth, like an engraver who never pressed harder in places. Make it small, though, and that spread-out tracking loses its drama next to Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong, whose high x-height and cracked-bangle rounds hold the page.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-palmyre: Noto Sans Palmyrene has curves that stop short of closing and ascenders cut compact. Stentiga then stretches out above it with straight-edged, constant strokes, so the page moves from tight to wide.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin: Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau reads open and modern, with curves that breathe. Across a long page its capitals sit only a short step above the lowercase, which keeps the lines low and quiet beneath Stentiga's blunt marker-tip heading.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Light, see-through and friendly up close. Noto Sans PhagsPa carries a long page easily, its open c shapes and gentle step up to capitals leaving Stentiga's round-rimmed heading to stand apart.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-phoenic: Stentiga looks like a bent steel rod, lean and luxurious, with its tracking pulled wide above a tall-lowercase body. Noto Sans Phoenician then reads easily, its s curves open at both ends.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-psalter: Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi reads friendly and direct, with gaping e shapes and capitals that barely rise. Its strongest quality is how quiet it stays under Stentiga, whose strokes never mix bold and light inside a single word.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Stentiga frames its counters in strokes of matching width. Down in the text, Noto Sans Rejang carries lowercase counters like wide glass portholes, so a long page of it stays open and easy on the eye.
